why: MET 2026-10-22 'Simple M1 fit at near-zero ages' and its follow-up the same evening. The sixth fit (05_fit6) is a separate run and is not changed by this one

scenarios: the time from adding TMSPA to the first acquisition taken as 0, 5 and 10 min ('0 min' is P. Broqvist's t = 0 at the first NMR). The first 31P spectrum of each tube still comes at its own offset from the first acquisition (3-5 min; 18.9 h in the 0.5 % tube). Only the first spectra of '2 % H2O', 'TMSPa alone' and 'TMSPa + TMSOH (A)' are sensitive to the age

structures: the chain M1 (one E0 per family, computed energies), M5 (the same barriers, energies of every independent reaction free) and M5-first (the main structure of the sixth fit: the first step of TMSPA apart in hydrolysis and transfer, energies free). Each step adds one thing: first the energies, then the barrier split. M1 is expected to fail on the equilibrium of the 2 % tube (fifth fit: chi2 729 of 886 there, MMSPA 0.07 predicted against 0.32), which no barrier, age or rule moves; it is read tube by tube

structures '+BEP': each of the three also with P. Broqvist's barrier rule, Delta G barrier = E0 downhill and E0 + Delta G uphill whichever way a step is written (capped BEP with alpha = 1, kinetics/fitting/candidates.py with_peter_bep), in every class including the exchange steps at 1.15 eV. M0-BEP (alpha = 0.5) is a different rule and is not fitted
energy_box_sigma: as in the sixth fit, every freed energy within 3 standard errors (MD) of its computed value, with the Gaussian cost inside the box

sample_overrides: as in the sixth fit (2 % tube heated 8 h at each step of its ramp; water of 'TMSPa alone' declared at the least its last spectrum needs, 65.6 mM); solvation EC/DEC 1:1 linear of the MD of the 8 Oct snapshot; network R1-R9 + N10-N15 (N12 and N15 take the hydrolysis barrier, the four exchanges a declared 1.15 eV); error model and fit rule (no |z| above 3) unchanged

effort: M1 has four parameters, so a dense search costs minutes (4096 screen points, 32 starts: twice the first plan, the user gave 10 h to finish M1). M5 and M5-first get the full search of the sixth fit at 0 min (8192 points, 32 starts) and a reduced one at 5 and 10 min (2048, 8), which also start from their own 0 min fit (scripts/run_fit.py runs the readings in the order 0, 5, 10 min). A '+BEP' structure takes the search of its Marcus form and also starts from it
start_from: none. The larger structures start from the smaller ones of this run (M1 -> M5 -> M5-first, embedded), not from earlier runs

night, for every structure of the run (the user: 'everything that may be interesting'; 10 h for M1, no limit for the rest): profiles of every parameter in every reading, whether the structure fits or not (for a structure that fails, the profile shows which parameters the data pin and how chi2 moves, not a confidence interval), with extra points at the interval edges; a profile minimum below the fit replaces it; leave-one-out in every reading, also where the structure fails (M1 without the 2 % tube: do the kinetic tubes fit with the computed energies?), with a stronger search than before (1024 points, 8 starts); the sensitivities below in every reading; solver tolerance (two profiles again at rtol 1e-8) for M1, M1+BEP, M5-first and M5-first+BEP at 0 min, on the barriers the first spectra pin (hydrolysis, transfer). No indistinguishability block (it is built on M3-split)

sensitivities: the declared error floor x0 and x2; the covariance of the computed energies x0.5 and x2 (skipped for M1, which frees no energy); the heating of the 2 % tube as the files record it, and 3 h of cooling before each of its rounds; the water of 'TMSPa alone' fitted instead of declared; N10-N15 all at 1.15 eV (Peter barriers); the 8 h at 80 C of the glovebox tube taken as 4 h and 16 h. A variant that fails on the reduced search is fitted again with the full one. '30 C before NMR 1' is left out: at a near-zero age there is no time before the first spectrum

recovery: one case per structure at 0 min, two seeds each, the truth being the run's own fit (kept in recovery/<case>_truth.json): if the tubes were exactly what the fit says, would the search and the profiles find it again? M1 with the search of its fits, the others with a reduced one (4096 points, 16 starts). It runs at the start of each night; a failure is reported and the night goes on (recovery_required false)
traces: every fit evaluated unchanged with 0 to 1 mM of TMSOH at mixing in the TMSPA tubes, and fitted again with 1 uM and 1 mM where it fits

predictions, for every structure and reading: tube B (hold-out), the 13C spectrum of tube A at 234 h (check), 'TMSPa alone' read from its first spectrum, the paper observations no fit uses (E4, 1 and 5 vol% water), storage at 25 C over the parameter sets accepted by the profiles, the bench protocol over the declared range of dS, and the trajectories of the TMSPA tubes from 36 s after mixing

order (run_chain.sh): phase 1, M1 and M1+BEP, every stage (fits, recovery, night, traces, predictions), to finish within 10 h; phase 2, the same stages for M5, M5-first and their '+BEP' forms (M1 is read back from its files), no time limit
